newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER-GILLES DE BILDE, BELGIUM'S FALLEN ANGEL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GILLES DE BILDE, BELGIUM'S FALLEN ANGEL.

text.p: Belgium reacted in disgust on Monday after its former soccer idol Gilles De Bilde was shown on nationwide television breaking another player's nose and eye by punching him in the face in a weekend league match.

"Gilles-the-disgrace," headlined Vers L'Avenir newspaper above a picture of De Bilde's victim, Aalst player Krist Porte, with his face, hands and jersey covered in blood. Others felt the incident had tarnished the reputation of Anderlecht and Belgian soccer and speculated it would end De Bilde's career in Belgium.

Soccer union president Michel D'Hooghe admitted the 25-year-old international striker's career was in jeopardy and his Anderlecht manager suggested he see a psychiatrist. The soccer union will discuss the incident next month when D'Hooghe intends to use the television pictures as evidence.

Porte, who also suffered slight concussion and possibly a torn retina and still might lose the eye, said on Sunday he had not decided yet whether to sue De Bilde although Aalst -- De Bilde's former club -- urged him to do so.
De Bilde shot to fame in Aalst with brilliant goals and dazzling dribbles and stole spectators' hearts with his boyish looks, radiant smile and sharp wit.
He became a national celebrity when he unexpectedly won the 1994 award for best Belgian league player and was a welcome guest on television talk and game shows.
He turned down a lucrative offer from Atletico Madrid and instead moved to Anderlecht, Belgium's most classy and prestigious team, because he first wanted to mature in Belgium.

He was never able to impress at Anderlecht and recently endured a growing barrage of criticism. Belgium coach Wilfried Van Moer dropped him from his squad for the World Cup qualifier against the Netherlands earlier this month.

De Bilde has also encountered a succession of personal problems which he says have made his life "hell for the past year and a half." His mother has been in an institution for neuropatients, his father suffered a severe brain haemorrhage last year, and he has come under increasing pressure at Anderlecht because of his below-par performances.
The incident occurred when Porte pulled De Bilde's shirt to try and prevent him from rushing towards goal as Anderlecht's Par Zetterberg took a penalty.
De Bilde wrestled himself free from Porte, turned half around and felled Porte with a left hook to the face in front of television cameras.
But the referee did not see the incident and De Bilde completed the match without even a warning. Anderlecht however suspended him until further notice on Sunday.

"I think that on a psychological level that boy is entitled to assistance. I think that perhaps he should have an open discussion with a specialist in psycholigacal affairs, perhaps more than one, to try and find his balance again," Anderlecht manager Michel Verschueren said.
De Bilde phoned Porte on Sunday to offer his apologies but Porte told him he did not want to see him, newspapers said.

De Bilde had already been in the legal limelight earlier this month when a court decided he should stand trial for assault after head-butting a male nurse and punching another last year when he was denied access to a hospital room where his father had been taken following his brain haemorrhage in August 1995.
He also received a suspended two-year jail sentence in 1992 for head-butting two boy scout leaders.
Aalst, who on Monday declined to comment on De Bilde, will not sue him but challenge the outcome of the game which they lost 3-0.
